body: English-like prose, which is what Brotli is actually for and what this probe has never had. Every other case here is a few hundred bytes of synthetic pattern, and the format's remaining ratio machinery -- context modelling, block splitting, the static dictionary -- all pay for a table once and earn it back over a long input. On a 540-byte cycle an extra literal tree costs more than it can ever return, so a corpus of small synthetic cases cannot tell those features from nothing.

author: reek
body: THE BYTES ARE WRITTEN OUT HERE RATHER THAN READ FROM OUR OWN CORPUS. Generating this input from BrotliDict would make the test circular -- a wrong corpus would produce a wrong input that our encoder and .NET's decoder would still have to agree on for the wrong reason. Written as literal ASCII, these are the real words whatever our copy says, so a corpus that drifted by one byte fails here.

author: reek
body: This is the case that proves the distance arithmetic against an INDEPENDENT copy of the corpus: .NET resolves each reference in its own dictionary, so a reference that decodes to the right bytes means our word ids and our position-dependent distances agree with a real implementation.
